assessment.nobel_worthiness: A rare chain from basic gut-hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 as an incretin and satiety signal) to therapies that transform type 2 diabetes and obesity management and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and its receptor, therapeutic proof of concept) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form, disputed in credit) are the discovery core. Knudsen's long-acting analogue chemistry is a real but industrial/translational contribution; the three-person limit forces a choice and credit for the active peptide remains debated.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent approved drugs, large outcome trials and wide clinical uptake over about two decades; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is contested and I have not independently verified the credit history.
Long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity and is used across the field; the conceptual and methodological impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth) are both decisive; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation complicates credit. Six credited people cannot fit in three slots, and I am uncertain about the fairest split.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: a decade and a half of independent, ubiquitous use, with first clinical steps in vision restoration.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation between discoverers of the channel and neuroscience implementers.
Therapeutic translation is still early, so the case rests on tool-based discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality; high clinical and conceptual impact in immuno-oncology.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain are central to costimulation-based CAR design and clinical proof; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. The original chimeric receptor concept (e.g. Eshhar) is not in the supplied credit, which I flag as a gap.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy; toxicity, access and solid-tumour limits are still evolving but do not undercut the core discovery.
uncertainties: Missing contributor in the supplied credited names weakens a fair configuration.
Long-term durability and secondary malignancy data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid synovitis and that blocking it controls disease, defining cytokine-targeted therapy for chronic inflammatory diseases. As an autoimmunity physician-scientist I regard the clinical transformation as real, but I apply the same criteria as for other fields.
assessment.attribution: A clear two-person pairing: Feldmann's mechanistic cytokine work in synovial cultures and Maini's clinical translation. Antibody engineering and others contributed but the core credit is relatively clean.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than 25 years of use, multiple agents, independent validation across diseases; recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee views this as a discovery of principle versus therapeutic development.
Biosimilar-era maturity is unquestionable; the question is only prioritisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent HPV infection and cervical precancer and are now reducing cervical cancer incidence at population level; a major cancer-prevention achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer contributed VLP work and the early development pathway. Other groups (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer) had contested contributions that are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly mature with population-level effectiveness data from multiple countries; timing is good.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over early VLP work are not resolved in the supplied text.
Prior prize recognition of HPV as a cause of cancer may influence perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy; a clear mechanism-to-cure example with deep RNA-biology originality.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and development) are a coherent two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical data; field-defining for RNA therapeutics but a younger story than several others.
uncertainties: Whether this is better recognised within a broader oligonucleotide-therapeutics framework.
Dependence on earlier antisense chemistry developments by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a regulator of cell survival (not proliferation) reshaped cell-death biology and cancer; venetoclax provides clinical validation.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams drove the cloning and functional program; Vaux showed survival function and cooperation with myc. Other key figures (Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto, Hockenbery, Strasser) are not all in the credited set or compete for slots.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with a clinical drug; apoptosis recognition by earlier prizes could make timing contested.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior apoptosis recognition and credit competition among BCL-2 pioneers.
Three-person limit forces exclusion of Strasser.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin and its therapeutic reactivation led to an approved gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia; strong genetics-to-therapy narrative.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A function and the human genetic link; Bauer contributed enhancer editing toward therapy. Thein's GWAS-based contributions are also material and compete for credit.
assessment.maturity: Therapy approved only recently, so long-term outcomes remain limited; basic discovery is well replicated, but recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Maturity of clinical outcomes and cost/access issues.
Competing credit from GWAS and other regulators of fetal globin.
